dedupe_keys.name: energy access explorer world resources institute open source geospatial platform for energy access planning

description: Energy Access Explorer is an open-source, online and interactive geospatial platform from the World Resources Institute that helps energy planners, clean energy enterprises, donors, development finance institutions and service delivery institutions identify high-priority areas for energy access interventions. For each geography it combines more than 50 geographic datasets on energy supply and demand, drawn from remote sensing and from global, national, sub-national and census sources that are public or provided by partners. Multi-criteria analysis of resource availability and infrastructure represents supply, while demographic data and data on social and productive uses represent demand; overlays, filters and buffer zones help prioritise areas for grid extension, off-grid systems, clean cooking and renewables. Coverage: the countries and sub-national areas loaded in the platform, which were not listed on the pages read; recent work covers Kenya, Tanzania, Uganda and districts in India. Format and access: an online map tool with tutorials, a technical note and a training course; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): MIT (website code); datasets under the WRI data platforms terms of use. Caveats: data quality depends on each partner's inputs. Simulation uses: siting and prioritising grid extension, mini-grids and service facilities in capacity planning for underserved areas. Related records: gridfinder (model-gridfinder) predicts distribution lines, and Open Infrastructure Map (data-open-infrastructure-map) shows mapped grids.
